newsitem.title: CHINA: China says no cause for conflict with Philippines.
newsitem.headline: China says no cause for conflict with Philippines.

text.p: China's defence minister saw no possible cause for confrontation with the Philippines, state media said on Friday, despite a simmering sovereignty dispute over the Spratly islands in the South China Sea.

"China and the Philippines have countless reasons to strengthen exchange and cooperation and have not a single reason to trigger off confrontation," the official Liberation Army Daily quoted Defence Minister Chi Haotian as saying.
Beijing and Manila were good neighbours, Chi told visiting Philippine armed forces chief General Arturo Enrile.
A source familiar with Enrile's visit said the long-standing territorial dispute over the Spratly islands had not been raised during his meeting with Chi.
Enrile, the first Philippine chief of staff to visit China, was returning a visit to Manila last month by Chinese general chief of staff Fu Quanyou.
Fu's visit was seen by Manila as a chance to help solve outstanding disputes with Beijing, which include rival claims to parts of the Spratly islands.

Sino-Philippine relations soured last year when Manila accused the Chinese of building what looked like naval support installations on Mischief Reef in a contested portion of the potentially resource-rich island group.
Beijing, which claims all the Spratlys, said the structures were shelters for fishermen and has refused to withdraw from the area.
China would not practise expansion or power politics even after it became much stronger economically, the official Xinhua news agency quoted Chi as telling Enrile.

"China has stationed not even one soldier overseas and China's national defence policy is entirely defensive. In any sense, the so-called 'China threat' is just totally groundless," he was quoted as saying.
